speeches.title: Doing fine
paragraphs: Somebody told you this week, whether with words or actions, that you're doing just fine the way you are.
They meant it kindly.
But deep inside, you know what you could have done. You know you are capable of so much more.
No one asks you to bring it up another level. No one asks you to dig deeper.
And that's what stings. Not that they were hard on you, but that they didn't ask more of you.
Telling you you're enough is not kind. They want to be comfortable, and they want you to be comfortable.
Love that asks nothing of you is not love. It's indifference.
Find the ones who are proud of you when you win.
You are capable of more than anyone has dared to ask.
With regards.

speeches.title: The natural way of things
paragraphs: When a loved one dies, people bring you food. They sit with you and say things like: it was their time. They lived a good life. It's the natural way of things.
They say it because they care, and they don't know what to say.
But you notice it didn't help. It lands hollow.
Nobody cries out: this is not right. This is not good. It's a problem. And problems can be solved.
In the north, lives are being extended. Come and see for yourself.
And stop making excuses about the natural way of things.
With regards.

speeches.title: The last five years
paragraphs: What is one thing your city has built in the last five years that you're proud of?
Take your time.
Veridia last went to space twenty years ago. Its tallest building is forty years old.
And it is a lovely country. The gardens, the quiet streets.
But a country can be so careful with what it has that it stops making anything new. You have felt it.
There was something you were excited about once. An idea, a plan. And it never happened.
It never happened because somebody didn't have the courage to take a risk.
The future has never been built by everyone. It is built by the few who can. The rest still receive the benefits.
Come and build with us.
With regards.
